thermal_charge_capacity.note: a complex scalar holds at most n_Q,max = n_Q(mu = M) in the gas; excess charge Bose-condenses

charge_in_thermal_plasma.note: evaluated at T_h ~ T_c in the restored phase (M = sqrt(Pi_X) T). For xi < xi_BEC the excess charge forms a homogeneous condensate whose phase structure is the charge_phase module's (H1/H2)

charge_after_thermal_restoration.note: if T_c/xi > T_n(r), i.e. xi < T_c/T_n(r), the charge density at the end of thermal restoration exceeds n_c (cold-sector placeholder) and phi = 0 persists until T_SM = T_n(r); the exit is then the charge route of charge_phase (spinodal at n_c, p(+) = p(-))

solitogenesis_estimate.note: estimate: Q per KZ volume at the spinodal exit (charge_phase xi_KZ, quoted) >> binding threshold, so charge-restored regions can leave bound Q-balls; with exact Z2 the surrounding vacuum signs are random

F_of_z.meaning: at fixed number density, Pi_phi ~ n^(2/3) Li2(z)/Li3(z)^(2/3) is largest at z = 1 (mu = 0): a bath with mu_N < 0 needs MORE quanta per T_c^3 to restore

restoration_number_bound.note: T_SM,min = minimum visible temperature at which a hidden population with relic yield <= Y_N_max can restore Z2 thermally (number conserved after restoration because 3->2 is inactive for xi <~ 3e-3, boltzmann.json). The condensate column uses the cold charged-condensate density n_c as a PLACEHOLDER for a coherent X population and is an estimate only

floor_inequality.statement: omega_h >= (m*|r|/m_b) omega_b + omega_sym (late-time dilute population: bound charge carries >= m* per unit, every other hidden quantum is a free NR particle of mass >= m_X); rigorous weaker form omega_h >= max[(m*|r|/m_b) omega_b, omega_sym]. Hence H_0 >= 100 sqrt(omega_b + omega_h,min + omega_sym) and the maser-envelope necessary condition becomes m_X|r| + (m_X/m*)(m_b/omega_b) omega_sym < 63.93 GeV (primary), 74.64 GeV (stress), with the envelope's conservative omega_b = 0.02125, m_b = 0.94738 GeV
floor_inequality.label: retrospective: omega_DM = 0.12 and the maser product bounds are known data (Codex 2ee7f82); not a prediction

charge_supply_cold_sector.condition: no charge-driven restoration iff n_Q(T_Q) = r Y_B s_SM(T_Q) < n_c, i.e. T_Q < T_n(r) = [n_c/(r Y_B (2 pi^2/45) g*s)]^(1/3) = 1.982e+05 r^(-1/3) (v/TeV) GeV
charge_supply_cold_sector.n_c_label: PLACEHOLDER (charge_phase T_h = 0 lower spinodal; its NOTES confirm 0.0316228 v^3)
charge_supply_cold_sector.v_scaling: T_n ~ v r^(-1/3); with r_max = 63.93 GeV/(gX v): T_n(r_max) = 2.301e+05 GeV (v/TeV)^(4/3)
charge_supply_cold_sector.note: valid for a homogeneously supplied charge in a cold (T_h << T_c) hidden sector with a pre-selected phi sign; supply below T_n is the charge_phase H2 case (fragmentation into Q-balls inside the sign-memory radius)

prior_art.ref: Frieman, Gelmini, Gleiser, Kolb, PRL 60 (1988) 2101; SLAC-PUB-4538/FERMILAB-PUB-88-013-A
prior_art.read: full preprint (OCR text of the Fermilab scan)
prior_art.detail: FLS potential with h|phi|^2(sigma - sigma0)^2 coupling and a sigma^3 term (a = lam2/lam1 = 0.15): Z2 explicitly broken, vacua non-degenerate; states that the exact-Z2 limit (h = lam2 = 0) gives stable domain walls that dominate unless sigma0 <~ 10 MeV; solitogenesis relies on the bias (pressure pinches false-vacuum regions); percolating case analysed only with bias

prior_art.read: preprint introduction and model section (OCR of scan; equations partly illegible)
prior_art.detail: same FGGK potential with lam2/lam1 = 0.15 (non-degenerate true vacuum); wall (surface) energy of the soliton ignored; statistical charge fluctuations as the charge source; no exact-Z2 wall analysis

prior_art.ref: Frieman, Olinto, Gleiser, Alcock, PRD 40 (1989) 3241; FERMILAB-PUB-89-128-A
prior_art.read: sections I-III and figure captions (OCR text) + abstract
prior_art.detail: generic NTS evolution (evaporation/accretion/freeze-out); formation discussed with schematic potentials having a unique true vacuum (metastable or unstable NTS phase at sigma = 0); 'pinch-off in the asymmetric vacuum model'; exact-Z2 domain walls not analysed

explicitly 'approximate' discrete symmetry: bias term A(phi) with vacuum splitting Lambda; notes exact Z2 walls would dominate (Zel'dovich-Kobzarev-Okun); analyses the biased (percolating) wall network following Gelmini-Gleiser-Kolb and its fragmentation into Fermi balls

tree potential lam(phi^2 - v^2)^2 + h^2 phi^2 |chi|^2 (same structure as Candidate 1); footnote: the phi -> -phi symmetry makes the model non-viable because of the domain-wall problem; assume explicit breaking or a charged phi; 'irrelevant for what follows'
confining field is the SM Higgs doublet (continuous gauged vacuum manifold, no discrete-vacuum walls); first-order EW transition with a singlet extension; no Z2 wall issue arises
dark-QCD first-order confinement/chiral transition; no real Z2 scalar; walls mentioned only for other authors' axion quark nuggets

prior_art.read: abstract + sections II and V (toy model)
prior_art.detail: generic Yukawa-trapped fermions; toy model U = (mu^2 + cT^2)phi^2/2 + mu3 phi^3/3 + lam phi^4/4 with a tree-level phi^3 (no Z2); a Z2 appears only as an R-parity-like stabiliser of the fermion, not of phi

prior_art_summary: None of the eight works analyses a persistent wall network of an EXACT Z2 in an FLS/Q-ball formation history. FGGK/GKM/FOGA, Ponton-Bai-Jain, Bai-Long-Lu and Hong-Jung-Xie use potentials without a degenerate Z2 (b); Macpherson-Campbell and Krylov-Levin-Rubakov keep the Z2 structure but break it explicitly (a), the former analysing the biased network (c). FGGK and Macpherson-Campbell state that the exact limit leads to the domain-wall problem. Candidate 1 forbids every such bias (BRIEF rule 5), so no prior-art mechanism removes its walls.
